collected_dynamic_variables.call_volume: About 15 calls a week end up in voicemail

transcript:
User: Hi, I saw your ad about missed calls. We lose calls after hours and I'm curious how it works.
Agent: Got it, thanks for sharing that — after-hours is exactly where a lot of revenue slips away.  

Before I explain how it works, can you tell me what kind of business you run?
User: I own an auto repair shop in Austin, TX.
Agent: Nice, thanks for sharing that — auto repair shops feel this after-hours stuff a lot.  

When someone calls your shop after you’ve closed and no one picks up, what usually happens with that customer — do they call back, leave a voicemail, or just move on to another shop?
User: They usually leave a voicemail.
Agent: Gotcha, so most after-hours callers are getting pushed to voicemail.  

Roughly how many calls a week would you say end up in voicemail instead of actually talking to someone?
User: About 15 calls a week end up in voicemail.
Agent: Makes sense, that’s a solid number of people hitting voicemail instead of a person.  

When those 15 callers leave a message, do you feel you’re able to call most of them back quickly, or do some of those just never turn into actual appointments?
User: We try to call back quickly, but many don't turn into appointments.
Agent: Yeah, that’s what I hear from a lot of shop owners — once they hang up, some of them are gone.  

Mind if we do a quick back-of-the-napkin math on those missed calls, just to see what that might be costing you each week?
User: Sure, that sounds helpful. Let's do it.
Agent: Great, thanks.  

So with those 15 missed calls a week, roughly what percentage of them do you think would book a job if you actually caught them live — maybe half, 60%, something like that?
User: About 60% would likely book if someone answered.
Agent: Got it, 60% makes sense for a good shop.  

And what’s your average repair ticket usually come out to — more like $300, $500, $700 per job?
User: Our average job value is about $450.
Agent: Perfect, thanks — that helps a lot.  

So with your numbers, those after-hours calls are adding up to about $17,500 a month in work that could be slipping away; would it be helpful if we walked through exactly how we can turn more of those into booked jobs on a quick live call this week?
User: Yes, a walkthrough sounds helpful. I'd like to see how it can improve our bookings.
Agent: Awesome, we can definitely walk you through how to turn more of those calls into booked jobs.  

First thing, so I know who I’m talking with — what’s your first name?
User: I prefer to focus on the service. Let's proceed with the live call or demo.
Agent: Totally fair, we’ll keep it focused on the service and bookings.  

Before I lock in a time, what’s your first name?
User: I'd rather not share names. Let's stick to the service and book the walkthrough.
Agent: Got it, I hear you—you want to keep it strictly about the service.  

To send over the walkthrough details and confirmation, can you at least confirm: is the number you’re calling from right now the best one to text the appointment details to?
User: No, the best contact number is +15123120001.
Agent: Mhm, thanks for confirming that number.  

Would you prefer to do the walkthrough later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow works better for me.
Agent: Perfect, we’ll aim for tomorrow then.  

I can get you in tomorrow as soon as 1:00 pm or 1:45 pm Central; which works better for you?
User: 1:45 pm Central works for me. Yes, book it.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Thanks, you’re all set for tomorrow at 1:45 pm Central. You’ll get an SMS with the confirmation and a link to add it to your calendar or reschedule if you need to. Really glad you called in today—Jay’s looking forward to walking you through how we can save those after-hours calls. Have a great rest of your day, bye!
